title.value: Proteins Sequence and Structure Co-Design with Equivariant Translation
title.justification: The title indicates the focus on protein design optimization using advanced translational techniques.
title.quote: P ROTEIN S EQUENCE AND S TRUCTURE C O -D ESIGN WITH E QUIVARIANT T RANSLATION

extractions.description: The paper presents a novel method for protein sequence and structure co-design, introducing an approach that allows for efficient and accurate iterative co-design of protein structures and sequences. This method leverages equivariant translation to enhance the speed and fidelity of protein design, which is crucial for biological and medical applications.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper primarily focuses on advancing protein design processes rather than directly addressing climate or ecological sustainability challenges.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Designing novel proteins with specific structures and desired functions has been a long-standing challenge in the field of bioengineering.

primary_category.justification: The paper does not align with any of the existing categories focused on climate or ecological sustainability.
primary_category.quote: Existing approaches generate both protein sequence and structure using either autoregressive models or diffusion models, both of which suffer from high inference costs.

secondary_categories.justification: The paper's aim at bioengineering and protein synthesis does not intersect with any predefined sustainability categories.
secondary_categories.quote: Proteins are macromolecules that perform essential functions in all living organisms.

primary_sub_category.justification: The paper does not focus on any known sub-categories within the remit of climate or ecological sustainable development.
primary_sub_category.quote: The task of protein sequence and structure co-design is the joint generation of residue types and 3D conformations.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: Secondary contributions are still within the bioengineering scope, which does not relate to sustainable development sub-categories.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: We conduct extensive experiments on the Structural Antibody Database (SAbDab) (Dunbar et al., 2014).

applications.value: Bioengineering protein structures and sequences more efficiently.
applications.justification: The applications focus is primarily on streamlining protein design technologies.
applications.quote: Numerical results show that our method outperforms previous state-of-the-art baselines and can generate high fidelity proteins in terms of both sequence and structure.

new_primary_category.justification: Though the paper introduces innovations in protein design, it does not align with climate or ecological sustainability disciplines.
new_primary_category.quote: The current focus on bioengineering optimization rather than environmental impacts justifies this classification.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: No new sub-category suggestions are necessary as it lies outside sustainability topics.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: Proteins can be viewed as chains of amino acids (residues) connected by peptide bonds.
